selected_proposals.selection_rationale: Primary strong-mechanism exploit: full PaiNN-style vector-conditioned body-order descriptor gate directly targets the source ISO17 energy/gap weakness while preserving the successful generation_016/proposal_002 body-order branch.
Tiny norm-only ablation of the same strong mechanism; isolates whether vector magnitude conditioning is enough with lower variance and implementation risk than the full norm-plus-dot gate.
Complementary low-risk exploit that modulates body-order residual amplitude rather than descriptor content, separating readout scaling from representation rewriting.
Architecture integration-path jump: moves body-order/vector information into the final scalar state so both main readout and residual paths can address ISO17 energy calibration.

Broader but still bounded PaiNNMixing jump on scalar/vector states, testing whether the strong evidence should be applied to the main learned representation rather than only the body-order side branch.

Backward simplification control for the source body-order message branch; important to determine whether the generation_016/proposal_002 improvement came from the added message pass or simpler static invariants would suffice.
Exact source control replicate for generation_016/proposal_002, required to interpret small G_delta changes against run variance.
Training-target diagnostic wildcard for the observed ISO17 late energy worsening; keeps architecture fixed and tests whether a tiny train.py-only schedule change explains part of the bottleneck.

selection_policy: Prioritize strong PaiNN-style vector/scalar mixing mechanisms from the generation_017 evidence package, cover exploit and jump integration paths, retain a backward-simplify branch and exact source control, and include one training-stability diagnostic for the ISO17 energy/gap failure mode.

omitted_proposals.reason: Dual-gated descriptor plus scalar residual coupling is a higher-interaction medium-risk combination; deferred until single-gate and main-state PaiNNMixing effects are measured.
Weak normalized l2 contraction stabilizer has weaker mechanism support and overlaps less directly with the strong M01 evidence than the selected vector-conditioning and training-diagnostic tests.
